name: Folk Strings of the World
sub: Six games. Eleven countries. One atlas of play.
text: Each instrument is drawn in detail and played by touch. Pluck and strum the twelve-string tiple and the big bass guitarron, draw the bow across the one-string gusle, the long string of the tromba marina, the horsehair strings of the jouhikko and the bells of the ravanahatha bow. Notes arrive along each string; touch them in time and hear the real voice of the instrument. A short note on every page tells where the tradition comes from and how it is played. Learn at your own pace: watch a demonstration first, read the rules and the how-to-play page, and enlarge the text if you like. Works in portrait and landscape. Try every instrument free for 90 seconds. One optional in-app purchase unlocks all of them for good. No subscription, no account and no internet connection needed.
